title: Al-Buruj: the Loving
hookLine: He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne (85:14–15)

cards: A trench, a fire, believers burned, and people sitting around it, watching. What comes after a story like that? Thunder would fit.

Something about justice, punishment, the scales set right. And the surah does say, a few verses on, that your Lord's grip is severe. But just after, it names Him with a word that's hard to expect there.
A tender word. The word for warm, close affection. Today: al-Wadud, the Loving.

teach.h: THE GRIP IS SEVERE. THEN THIS.
teach.b: Verse twelve: the grip of your Lord is severe. Verse thirteen: He is the one who begins creation and brings it back. And verse fourteen, in Pickthall's words: "And He is the Forgiving, the Loving."
Then: Lord of the Throne, the Glorious. Al-Ghafur, the Forgiving, then al-Wadud, the Loving.
Wadud comes from wudd, warm affection, the love between people who are close: the hand on the shoulder, the meal saved for you.
In Surah nineteen the Qur'an promises that the Merciful will place wudd among those who believe and do good.

And it uses al-Wadud as a name of God only twice: here, and in Surah eleven, where the prophet Shu'ayb tells his people: ask forgiveness, turn back, my Lord is Merciful, Loving. Both times it sits next to forgiveness.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO LOVES, AND IS LOVED.
teach.b: Some scholars note the form can run two ways: the One who loves, and the One who is loved. God loves His servants, and is loved by them. Now look at where it's placed.
Right after the persecutors in the ditch, and right after verse ten, which said the punishment is for those who then did not repent.
The door left open yesterday has a name on it today. The fire in the trench was real. So is this.

Al-Wadud is counted among the ninety-nine names of God, and some call on it when they pray for love between people: between spouses, between families that have drifted, between hearts that have gone cold.

how: Al-Wadud is counted among the ninety-nine names of God; ya Wadud is often said in personal prayer, especially when asking for love and reconciliation between spouses, families and friends.

o: the Loving, a name of God for warm affection
the Patient, who waits before He punishes
the Forgiving, who pardons those who turn back

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.
p: Shu'ayb: my Lord is Merciful, Loving

s: al-Wadud appears as a name of God only twice in the Qur'an
here in 85:14, and in 11:90, both times beside forgiveness or mercy.
Al-Buruj follows the people of the ditch only with threats
it says the grip is severe, then names Him the Forgiving, the Loving.
wadud can mean both the one who loves and the one who is loved
scholars note the form can run both ways.

games.q: right after the story of the ditch and the severe grip, which two names does Al-Buruj give?
games.why: al-Ghafur, al-Wadud (85:14). after a hard story, two tender names, with forgiveness first.

practice: Think of a time love was shown to you: not a feeling, a thing someone did, a meal, a ride at 3am, a note, a hand held in a hospital. Let the memory be clear, and notice that it was love that did something.
If you pray, you can say ya Wadud, O Loving One, three times, slowly.

wordCard.voice: Al-Wadud. The Loving, the One who loves and is loved, named in Surah eighty-five right after the Forgiving. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Loving, from w-d-d, warm affection; a name of God in 85:14 and 11:90.

carryVoice: Your line: the loving one. Forgiving first, and then Loving. Two hundred five days in.
